description: Tests whether homogeneous punctuation dependence or persistent dialogue/narration switching can reproduce the length-dependent human G-statistic overdispersion.

pre_registration.freeze_instruction: After manual segmentation validation, review this file, set status to frozen_before_simulation, and commit or externally timestamp it before the inferential run. Engineering smoke runs must use explicit bypass settings and are not evidence.
pre_registration.claim: Sufficiency, not uniqueness: compare homogeneous oracle and finite-reference processes with a two-state discourse process fitted without the evaluation authors.

segmentation.rule: quote-delimited spans; quote marks belong to dialogue; quote state resets at blank-line paragraph boundaries
segmentation.nested_quotes: stack directional and symmetric quote pairs
segmentation.tokenization: apply the frozen full-text spaCy tokenizer after Gutenberg stripping and ellipsis normalization; only exact quote tokens can change state
segmentation.apostrophes: standalone straight apostrophe tokens follow the frozen parser and are treated as symmetric quote marks; apostrophes embedded in contraction tokens do not change state
segmentation.unmatched_closer: retain current state and record an error
segmentation.unclosed_quote: close at paragraph boundary and record it
known_limitations: quotes glued into a larger spaCy token are neither extracted nor used as state boundaries
title-page and metadata quotations remaining after boilerplate removal are treated like prose quotations
OCR-damaged and elision-like standalone apostrophes can be misclassified and are assessed by the blinded manual sample

manual_validation.sampling: 100 marks per automatic state, shuffled; automatic labels withheld from the annotation file

evaluation.parameter_training: all books from the other four author folds
evaluation.reference_design: two synthetic whole books scored against one synthetic target, matching each real three-book rotation

iid.prediction: phi approximately one with an oracle reference; finite-reference growth is measured separately

markov.prediction: f3 phi approaches one with an oracle reference; finite-reference growth is measured separately

two_state_hsmm.prediction: persistent discourse-state switching can produce approximately linear f3 phi growth

estimands.sampling_frame: At each n, human phi pools every complete non-overlapping chunk. Each simulated observation independently samples one entry uniformly from that exact book-by-chunk frame, generates through the selected chunk position, and scores that chunk. This gives books probability proportional to their number of observed chunks and includes 60/59/56 books at n=1000/2000/4000.
estimands.phi_n: pooled-chunk mean G divided by nominal feature degrees of freedom
estimands.rho_at_n: (phi(n)-1)/n, reported separately at every chunk size to diagnose f1 versus f3 drift
estimands.fixed_intercept_rho: least-squares slope of phi(n)-1 on n with intercept fixed at one
estimands.implied_delta: rho times degrees of freedom divided by two
estimands.raw_delta: G/(2n) for f1 and G/(2(n-1)) for f3
estimands.excess_delta: (G-df)/(2n), the observation-level estimator corresponding to E[G]=df+2n*delta
estimands.tail: CV and Fisher-Pearson skew for signed excess_delta; two-sample KS distance, Wasserstein distance, negative mass and upper quantiles compare human and fitted-point distributions without imposing positive support. A moment-matched gamma KS distance is descriptive and applies only to positive raw_delta.
estimands.human_uncertainty: author-cluster bootstrap percentile interval for pooled-chunk mean G and phi
estimands.monte_carlo_uncertainty: normal 95% interval for each simulated mean plus empirical 2.5% and 97.5% observation quantiles
